 Draymond Green (elbow) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Magic. 
 Green has an inflamed right elbow. If he can’t play on Saturday, the Warriors may turn to Georges Niang to fill the resulting void in the starting lineup. 
 Will Richard 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Will Richard started on Thursday and finished with 10 points (4-of-6 FGs), one rebound, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Heat. 
 Richard got the starting nod for the second straight game and for the third time this season. Multiple players have filled out the fifth starting spot with Jimmy Butler III (knee) sidelined to start the year. Richard only played 16 minutes in this game, with Georges Niang and Brandon Williams each surpassing 20 minutes and scoring in double figures. Richard may continue to start, but he isn’t worth adding off the waiver wire. 
 Draymond Green 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Draymond Green was ejected from Monday’s game against the Suns with 10 minutes left in the third quarter. 
 Green picked up two technical fouls early in the third quarter. After Suns center Khaman Maluach bumped him, Green got up, wrapped up Maluach, and threw him to the ground. The second technical was assessed when Green got into it with Dillon Brooks, who also received a technical foul. Green (4/4/2/1) was replaced in the lineup by Charles Bassey. 
 Gui Santos 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #15 
 Gui Santos (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Santos did not play in the second half of Sunday’s win over the Clippers, finishing with four points, three rebounds, one assist and one block in nine minutes. Following the victory, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said that the team will re-evaluate Santos, whose knee tendinitis remains an issue. At a minimum, he’ll miss Monday’s game, which could mean more playing time for Georges Niang

 Larry Nance Jr. shot 5-of-7 from the field in Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets, scoring 15 points with two rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers.
 Nance was in a groove on Saturday, matching his career high with five three-pointers. The veteran forward/center needed just seven attempts to reach that mark, a welcome development after Nance began the season shooting 5-for-17 from deep. He still can’t be relied on in most fantasy leagues, but Nance played 13 minutes while fellow reserve Jay Huff (zero points, three rebounds) played 10 minutes.

 Player Stats

 Ivica Zubac tallied 10 points (4-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds and five assists in Saturday’s loss to the Pacers.
 For the third time in five games and the first time since October 23, Zubac hit double figures in rebounds. He missed five games with a sprained ankle, so the 7-footer is still finding his footing. And it doesn’t help that Tyrese Haliburton is out with a strained hamstring. That absence has negatively impacted the Pacers offensively, and Zubac attempted just five shots on Saturday. The Pacers play four games next week, starting with the Mavericks on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Pascal Siakam accumulated 23 points (10-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets.
 Siakam has scored at least 20 points in seven of nine games this season, including Saturday’s effort in Mexico City. Unfortunately, the Pacers forward’s production hasn’t led to wins, as Indiana has lost five of its last six games since Tyrese Haliburton suffered a strained hamstring. Siakam and the Pacers play four games next week, starting with the Mavericks on Monday.
